html:
The Polans, or Polianians, were an East Slavic tribe living on both banks of the middle Dnieper around Kyiv, from about the 500s to the 800s. They are on the map for 900.

The Primary Chronicle praises them as gentle and lawful, and tells the legend that Kyiv was founded by three brothers, Kyi, Shchek and Khoryv, and their sister Lybid. For a time the Polans paid tribute to the Khazars. In 882 the Varangian Oleg took Kyiv and made it his capital, and the Polan land became the core of Kievan Rus'. Their neighbours included the Severians to the east. They should not be confused with the Polans of Poland.
